items.content:
Ghost Identifier

  • Bhoot's unique abilities will now properly display in the Ghost Identifier.

    [/*]

  • Demon's unique abilities will now properly display in the Ghost Identifier.

    [/*]

  • Tariaksuq's unique abilities will now properly display in the Ghost Identifier.

    [/*]

  • Forgotten's unique abilities will now properly display in the Ghost Identifier.

    [/*]

Cameras

  • Cameras will now start in IR Mode by default.

    [/*]

  • Opening the Phantom Detect app will display the last camera you were viewing

    [/*]

Custom Difficulty Modifier

  • You can now select a forced ghost type under custom difficulty settings.

    Specific Ghost: If you select a specific ghost, you are guaranteed to get that ghost. Prefer New: New ghost types have an increased chance of being selected, but not guaranteed. None: All ghost types have an equal chance of being selected.

    • Selecting a specific ghost will not allow you to receive rewards for that game, nor will it unlock the ghost in your guide.

      [/*]
    [/*]

Cellphone

  • Added a Hot Key for the Cellphone Flash (by default, "L")

    [/*]

Ghost Guide

  • Added a Ghost Guide app to the laptop.

    [/*]

  • Players can now view both locked and unlocked ghosts from the Ghost Guide.

    [/*]

  • Unlocked ghosts will display their name.

    [/*]

  • Locked ghosts will continue to display as "???".

    [/*]

  • The Ghost Guide will now keep track of how many times you've successfully identified each ghost.

    [/*]

Ghost Changes

  • Puca can now copy 12 distinct hunting behaviors from other ghosts during hunts.

    [/*]

HQ

  • Added several new items for players to decorate and customize their HQ.

    [/*]

  • Added Fish Tanks and Terrariums as new HQ customization options.

    [/*]

Content Creator Program

  • Fixed all Content Creator Brand Kits.

    [/*]

QoL:

  • Map selection randomness has been adjusted to allow for less Abaddon Hallows.

    [/*]

items.title: Version 0.9.8.1 - Orbs and Apparitions
items.summary: 7 New Ghosts Seven new entities have made their way to The Other Side , each bringing their own behaviors and characteristics to uncover: Ataphoi [/*] Hupia [/*] Marid [/*] Nasnas [/*] Puca [/*] Sluagh [/*] Wiederganger [/*] Ghost Orbs Are
items.content:
7 New Ghosts

Seven new entities have made their way to The Other Side, each bringing their own behaviors and characteristics to uncover:

  • Ataphoi

    [/*]

  • Hupia

    [/*]

  • Marid

    [/*]

  • Nasnas

    [/*]

  • Puca

    [/*]

  • Sluagh

    [/*]

  • Wiederganger

    [/*]

Ghost Orbs Are Here

Ghost Orbs have been added as a brand-new evidence type!

Ghost Orbs are normally invisible to the naked eye and can only be seen using infrared vision, adding another reason to keep an eye on your cameras.

  • Ghost Orbs are normally only visible through infrared vision.

    [/*]

  • Orbs can also be photographed using the cellphone camera flash.

    [/*]

New Remote Camera System

A new remotely viewable camera has been added, giving investigators another way to monitor paranormal activity from a safer distance.

  • Supports both visible light and infrared modes.

    [/*]

  • Infrared mode can be used to spot Ghost Orbs.

    [/*]

  • Camera modes can be changed remotely from the vehicle laptop.

    [/*]

  • Live feeds can be viewed through the Phantom Detect app.

    [/*]

New Equipment: Wireless Camcorder

The new Wireless Camcorder can be mounted directly to a tripod for easier placement and monitoring.

  • The Wireless Camcorder can be mounted to the tripod.

    [/*]

  • The tripod can be picked up and carried while the camera remains attached.

    [/*]

Dynamic Light Detection

Lighting now has a much more direct impact on both players and paranormal activity.

Players are now given a dynamic Light Contribution Score based on how illuminated they actually are, rather than simply whether they are standing inside a room with the lights on.

  • The more illuminated you are, the slower your anxiety increases.

    [/*]

  • Standing directly near a light source provides more protection than simply being somewhere in a lit room.

    [/*]

  • Multiple nearby light sources can contribute to your overall illumination.

    [/*]

  • Your score updates dynamically as you move through the environment or lighting conditions change.

    [/*]

Ghosts can also react to lighting in new ways. Depending on the ghost and the situation, light may now influence its behavior, creating new reasons to consider where you're standing, which lights are active, and how much darkness surrounds you.

Cellphone UI Overhaul

The Phantom Detect app has received a complete UI overhaul!

  • Environmental CCTV cameras can now be viewed directly from the cellphone.

    [/*]

  • Added support for viewing feeds from the new Wireless Camcorder.

    [/*]

  • Redesigned the interface to make navigating between available camera feeds cleaner and easier.

    [/*]

Identifier App

The Identifier app has also received a major visual and information overhaul.

  • The main ghost selection screen now has a much cleaner layout.

    [/*]

  • Ghost information pages now include behavioral information.

    [/*]

  • Behavioral information can be unlocked after successfully identifying that ghost type.

    [/*]

The more ghosts you successfully identify, the more you'll learn about what makes each one unique.

Hunt & Network Improvements

We've made several improvements to synchronization during hunts and other rapidly changing paranormal events.

Photo Synchronization

  • Added time synchronization and lag compensation when taking photos.

    [/*]

  • Photo capture timing is now synchronized between players, helping ensure rapidly changing paranormal events are represented consistently for everyone involved in the capture.

    [/*]

Hunt Flicker Synchronization

  • Added time synchronization and lag compensation to ghost flickering during hunts.

    [/*]

  • Hunt flickers are now synchronized between players, greatly reducing situations where a ghost could appear visible to one player while being invisible to another at the same moment.

    [/*]

Hunt Cooldown

  • Hunt cooldowns are now stopped when a forced hunt is activated after disorientation.

    [/*]

Hunt Lighting

  • Lights that are already off now flicker at a much lower intensity while the ghost is hunting.

    [/*]

Ghost Behavior Adjustments

Behavior adjustments have been made to several existing ghost types:

  • Wisp

    [/*]

  • Strigoi

    [/*]

  • Forgotten

    [/*]

  • Demon

    [/*]

  • Bhoot

    [/*]

Keep an eye out - you may find that some familiar ghosts don't behave quite the way you remember.

Evidence Changes

  • EMF is no longer included as passive evidence in Identify.

    [/*]

Breakers & Lighting

We've made several adjustments to how ghosts interact with the investigation site's electrical system.

  • Adjusted how frequently ghosts interact with the breaker panel.

    [/*]

  • Ghosts can now turn the breaker on.

    [/*]

  • Light switches that were not directly interacted with no longer play their interaction sound when their state changes.

    [/*]

Equipment & Placement

Equipment placement should now feel more natural and predictable.

  • Placing equipment now begins with the item facing toward or away from the player as appropriate.

    [/*]

  • When picking up furniture in the HQ, its existing orientation is now preserved when the placement preview begins.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Fixed the Stopwatch app keybind not working while dead.

    [/*]

  • Fixed players being able to interact with the environment while the cellphone was focused.

    [/*]

  • Players can no longer take photos of UV stains without a UV light/stick present.

    [/*]

Between 7 new ghosts, Ghost Orbs, the Wireless Camcorder, revamped cellphone apps, dynamic lighting, new ghost behaviors, and multiplayer synchronization improvements, there's a lot more to discover during your investigations.

See you on The Other Side!

The silence was the worst part. Not the sudden silence of elk themselves, but the silence right after the shot, that sudden crushing, anxiety-filled pit in my stomach. For the entire morning of September 21st, the river bottom I was hunting was a chaotic, screaming, bugling rut fest. Now, the big satellite bull, the one I had just wounded with a poorly placed arrow, had vanished into the head-high marsh grass. The herd had fallen quiet, melting away into the dark jungle of aspens and cottonwoods on the other side of the stubble field.

I stood there, my heart hammering against my ribs, a cold knot of regret tightening in my stomach. The "fifty-yard single-pin strategy," a technique I had only seen described online and had never actually practiced, suddenly felt like a profound self-betrayal.

I raised my binoculars, hands still shaking, and picked him up at eight hundred yards. Through the glass, I could see the fresh, red stain running down his right side, starting just below his withers. He was moving, bugling, and very much alive. The shame of a poorly placed shot was corrosive. The entire season, a lifetime of planning, and a sixteen-year wait for this specific tag now felt tainted by a single, high, limited-penetration mistake.

As a kid in the 1980s, my world was bounded by my Montana hometown and the old family homestead that sat halfway up the dirt road leading to a historic ghost town. I spent my summers wading in the cold waters of the creek that ran below our family cabin, catching small, wild brook trout, and exploring the granite boulders stacked like Legos in the hills above.

One of my most distinct memories of this place as a kid was drinking water directly out of a steel pipe my family had set up to collect the cold spring water seeping directly out of the mountain. As a child, I didn't grasp the unique history of this landscape; it was simply my playground. I didn't truly discover its pull until the summer of 2016, when I climbed a hill in our meadow to scatter my mother's ashes alongside my father's.

When I opened my email in mid-summer of 2025 to find I had drawn the coveted bull elk tag for a nearby unit, the weight of the past came rushing back. I hunted it before in 2009 but spent that entire season on the other side of the range, relying on leads from friends and never even considering the mountains behind our own property. The math of drawing this tag a second time was brutal; even with sixteen bonus points, my odds were barely three percent. The pressure that came with that number wasn't just about the search for a trophy; it was about honoring a multi-generational connection to this specific mountain range.

My family's roots here are literally etched into the earth. My grandfather, Wade V. Lewis Sr., a mining engineer, appropriated a claim for silver and lead in 1924. Twenty-five years later, he and two partners discovered radioactivity at the abandoned site, and when a visiting investor's wife found her chronic bursitis pain vanished after a few visits underground, word spread fast. What began as the Free Enterprise Uranium Mine, Montana's first, became the state's original radon health mine, a business my father ran for a time and my nephew Ryan still runs today.

On the other side of town, deeper into the mountains, lies the ghost town, a place of triumph and quiet tragedy. A Swiss immigrant named Peter Wys discovered silver here in 1868 and died mysteriously within a few years of the find. Norwegian entrepreneur Anton M. Holter acquired the claim in 1875 and developed the Holter Lode; by the late 1880s the town had boomed to 2,500 people.

Unlike the rowdy bachelor camps common to early Montana mining, this was a town for families with schools, churches, and the Fraternity Hall, built in 1893 and still standing today as part of Montana's smallest state park. It was a hard place to live; water was scarce and woodcutters stripped the surrounding hillsides bare to feed the stamp mills. The forest cemetery holds the quietest testament to that hardship: dozens of children's headstones, casualties of the brutal winter of 1888 and the diphtheria epidemic that followed. By 1931, the mines had gone silent and the rails were pulled up. Today, a handful of local families work to preserve what's left.

Our family property is not an old mining claim, as I'd always assumed. It was a homestead, carved out under the Forest Homestead Act of 1906. A Forest Service surveyor named Raymond Mauren walked our meadow in April of 1915, dragging his brass chains to map the boundaries out of what was then the Helena National Forest, and the land was patented to a man named George Walker the following spring. The small, one-room cabin on the property, now claimed by packrats, wasn't a miner's bunkhouse; it was Walker's home, likely built between 1913 and 1915. It's humbling to think this meadow once cleared by one man with a crosscut saw and a horse now serves as our sanctuary, where my parents' ashes rest in soil worked by hand over a century ago.

In the years leading up to drawing this tag, my wife Jen and I spent our summers running a rather large circuit of game cameras on the ridges above the property. We didn't do it with any real expectation of drawing the tag. We did it because we loved the land and wanted to know the wild neighbors we shared it with. It was about learning the terrain, discovering preferred trails, and understanding how the animals used this specific pocket of the mountains.

Through those cameras, we got to know the resident animals by name: Hank the Tank, a massive cinnamon-phase black bear; the non-shedding, hormone-addled "Cactus Bull"; Big Six, a large six-point with enormous whale tails; and a pair of six-point bulls we called Tall Guy and Wide Guy. Wide Guy was what I dream of when I think about bull elk: wide, symmetrical, and heavy, with long sweeping thirds and distinct, aggressively hooked brow tines. He was a digital ghost we watched grow season after season but had never seen in person, a theoretical target we never seriously expected to chase.

Over the years, those cameras taught us a critical lesson: our local elk almost always cleared out of our timber during the chaotic September rut, only filtering back into these drainages once the pressure of rifle season got underway. We tried to figure out their internal clocks, their preferred escape routes, and exactly where they were most likely to materialize. Those preseason images of Wide Guy kept me dreaming. He set the standard.

items.title: What's coming next?
items.summary: What's Next? The Custom Difficulty Update launched just over a week ago, but we're already hard at work on what's coming next. New Ghosts Our next major update introduces 7 brand-new ghost types for Identify , each inspired by real-world fo
items.content:
What's Next?

The Custom Difficulty Update launched just over a week ago, but we're already hard at work on what's coming next.

New Ghosts

Our next major update introduces 7 brand-new ghost types for Identify, each inspired by real-world folklore and designed with unique behaviors that will challenge even experienced investigators.

Nas Nas

Known for its relentless speed, the Nas Nas darts and lunges with unpredictable bursts of movement, losing distances in an instant, and turning any encounter into a race.

Ataphoi

A restless spirit from ancient Greek lore, believed to bring misfortune and sickness to the living. Investigators report rarely seeing the Ataphoi in full form.

Hupia

A spirit from Tino folklore, the Hupia is a nocturnal spirit, known to be incredibly active after-dark. Investigators report feeling ill-prepared for the aggression the Hupia shows.

Wiederganger

A spirit that returns to the living world with unfinished business, the Wiederganger is tied to vengeance, or unrest, bringing increased dread to those who seek it out.

Marid

A powerful spirit from Arabic folklore, the Marid is believed to wield great supernatural influence, bringing misfortune and twisting outcomes to those who encounter it.

The Sluagh

A host of restless spirits in Irish and Scottish folklore, said to travel together as a dark force.

The Púca

Known for its unpredictable and mischievous nature, often toying with the living for its own amusement.

Each ghost will have their own behaviors, unique to their real-life lore.

New Equipment & Evidence

Alongside these new ghosts comes one of our most requested additions.

Wireless Camcorder

The Wireless Camcorder will allow investigators to monitor locations remotely, working seamlessly with our surveillance systems to open up new investigative strategies.

Ghost Orbs

Ghost Orbs are joining the evidence roster, but not in the way you might expect. Rather than feeling like simple floating particles, we're designing them to behave naturally and feel genuinely unsettling when spotted.

Two New Locations

The McGavin House

Explore a beautifully preserved early 19th-century home where history and horror intertwine. Though officially remembered as the estate of an unsolved murder, those willing to dig a little deeper may discover that the truth has been waiting nearly two centuries to be uncovered.

Blackmeadow Farm

Nestled in the countryside, The Blackmeadow Farm has been home to the same family for generations. Recently however, unexplained disturbances have transformed daily life into a nightmare. Strange noises echo through the barn after dark, shadows moving through the halls, and the family insists they are no longer alone.

Why the Wait?

We know many of you are eager to jump into this update, and so are we... But these aren't features we want to rush.

Every ghost is being carefully designed to stay as faithful as possible to the folklore that inspired it. Ghost Orbs are receiving extra attention to ensure they feel believable rather than distracting, and the Wireless Camcorder is being built to integrate naturally into the investigation experience.

We'll announce a release date once we're confident the update is ready.

Trust us, this one will be worth the wait.

Version 0.9.8.0_b

items.title: 10 Games to Play if You Love MECCHA CHAMELEON
items.summary: MECCHA CHAMELEON is a fantastic hide-and-seek game, but there are plenty of other titles for you to check out.
items.content:
By Aden Carter Published Jun 17, 2026, 8:30 AM EDT Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles.

Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant , XDA , Gamepur , Impulse Gamer , and WePC . He currently also works with GameSandwich and VideoGamer , where he handles guide content, news, and reviews for the latest games. Across his games writing career, he has worked as a freelance writer and editor, with experience reviewing around 40 games and interviewing multiple indie developers. Aden holds a B.A. in Creative Writing for Entertainment .

on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap MECCHA CHAMELEON is not the first hide-and-seek game on the market, but it has managed to catch the attention of thousands, as its unique painting mechanic stands out.

Instead of hiding normally, you get to paint yourself into your environment, making things a bit more difficult. It is a unique take on a classic game genre, and it makes it that much more fun to play.

Forget blockbuster AAA games! We want some plucky little indies!

If you have found yourself going back to MECCHA CHAMELEON over and over again, you might want to check out some of these other titles that offer the same type of hide-and-seek action, but in a different way.

Expand Collapse Midnight Murder Club is a very fun title created by Velan Studios, and it is designed to give you a crazy shooter experience inside a massive mansion. You and your friends enter a mansion, each armed with a pistol. The catch is that everything is pitch black, making it a large game of hide-and-seek where the objective is to find and kill each other.

You have a flashlight that you can use to find your way, and you will need it, as it is impossible to see without it. Of course, using this flashlight will help others see you as well.

To add to the chaos, there are various game mode modifiers that allow you to change how the game is played. Some cards add the ability to shoot through walls, and others allow you to shrink. Some even cause loud jazz music to play when you shoot your pistol.

Expand Collapse Have you ever been in a fight with a friend or sibling while playing a local PvP game and been accused of screencheating or screenpeaking? Well, the game Screencheat requires you to do this.

Screencheat is like a big game of hide-and-seek, but the catch is that you are all shooters who are invisible. Just looking at your screen will not help you find anyone. That is why everyone else's screens appear as well.

You are meant to look at the other screens that appear as split-screen style on your own to determine where each player is and take them out. It definitely puts a new spin on the shooter genre and gives it that hide-and-seek feeling.

Expand Collapse Among Us became a massive hit a few years back, and there are plenty of people who still play it to this day, and for good reason. It is a social deduction game where the killer needs to blend in, take out their crewmates, and then make everyone believe it was someone else.

While it is not necessarily a hide-and-seek title, the game shares some similarities with the genre, where the killer needs to remain hidden and not be sussed out by the other crewmates.

items.title: Custom Difficulty | Version 0.9.8.0
items.summary: Version 0.9.8.0 - Custom Difficulty Update Hello Investigators, Version 0.9.8.0 introduces one of the largest gameplay customization updates we've released so far. With the new Custom Difficulty System , you'll be able to tailor investigati
items.content:
Version 0.9.8.0 - Custom Difficulty Update

Hello Investigators,

Version 0.9.8.0 introduces one of the largest gameplay customization updates we've released so far. With the new Custom Difficulty System, you'll be able to tailor investigations to match your preferred playstyle, whether you're looking for a casual ghost hunt or a brutal challenge that pushes your team to its limits.

This update also includes a highly requested Headbob Reduction option, inventory improvements, contract selection enhancements, gameplay adjustments, and a variety of fixes.

Custom Difficulty System

The new Custom Difficulty System allows you to customize nearly every aspect of an investigation.

Adjust ghost behavior, hunt settings, evidence availability, player limitations, rewards, and much more. Reward multipliers will scale based on your selected settings, allowing you to create your own unique challenge.

False Evidence (Identify)

On higher difficulties, ghosts can now leave behind False Evidence.

False evidence initially appears as the strongest form of evidence before gradually degrading over time.

Examples:

  • Audio 3 → Audio 2 → Audio 1

    [/*]

  • UV 3 → UV 2 → UV 1

    [/*]

  • Writing 3 → Writing 2 → Writing 1

    [/*]

When investigating, you'll need to decide whether to:

  • Rule out the ghost using its behaviors

    [/*]

  • Wait for suspicious evidence to degrade before making a final decision

    [/*]

Evidence Breakdown

Novice

  • 3 Real Evidence

    [/*]

  • No False Evidence

    [/*]

Intermediate

  • 3 Real Evidence

    [/*]

  • No False Evidence

    [/*]

Expert

  • 2 Real Evidence

    [/*]

  • 1 False Evidence

    [/*]

Master

  • 1 Real Evidence

    [/*]

  • 2 False Evidence

    [/*]

Favorite Room Changes

Ghosts can now change their favorite room during an investigation.

Frequency varies by difficulty:

  • Intermediate: Low Chance

    [/*]

  • Expert: Medium Chance

    [/*]

  • Master: High Chance

    [/*]

When this occurs, the previous favorite room will not immediately return to normal temperatures. Instead, it will slowly warm back up over several minutes.

Keep monitoring the location carefully. The room you started in may not be the room you finish in.

Continuous Hunts After Death

With this modifier enabled, successfully killing a player will immediately restart the hunt timer.

The hunt doesn't end simply because someone died.

Shared Consequences

With this modifier enabled, if one investigator dies, the entire team dies.

This includes teammates who are outside of the huntable location.

Random Door Lockdowns

On higher difficulties, ghosts may occasionally lock nearby doors.

  • Up to 2 doors can be locked at once

    [/*]

  • Eligible doors are selected near the ghost's favorite room

    [/*]

  • Doors remain locked for 30–45 seconds

    [/*]

  • The ghost can still initiate hunts while doors are locked

    [/*]

Don't get trapped.

Random Tarot Card Effects

When enabled, each player begins the contract with a random tarot card effect.

Possible effects include:

  • Sleepy

    [/*]

  • Squeaky Feet

    [/*]

  • Blurry Vision

    [/*]

  • Random Screams

    [/*]

  • Butter Fingers

    [/*]

Each player receives their own effect, meaning teammates may begin the contract with entirely different conditions.

Adjustable Inventory Capacity

Customize how many items players can carry at once.

Available options:

  • 1 Item

    [/*]

  • 2 Items

    [/*]

  • 3 Items

    [/*]

  • 4 Items

    [/*]

Headgear is not affected by this setting.

Forced Evidence

Certain ghosts now have evidence types that will always appear when evidence is limited.

This does not apply to Zero Evidence configurations.

Create Your Own Challenges

Custom Difficulty isn't limited to the built-in presets. You can create and save up to 13 custom difficulty configurations, each with their own unique rules, restrictions, and reward multipliers.

Build your own challenge modes, experiment with unusual settings, or create custom presets tailored for different groups of friends. Once saved, your presets can be selected at any time from the difficulty menu.

From casual investigations to nightmare fuel, the choice is yours.

Heart Rate System Adjustments

You'll notice that the Starting Heart Rate modifier includes values that differ from the previous versions. This is because the entire heart rate system has been rebalanced.

New Heart Rate Range

Previous:

  • 80 BPM → 140 BPM

    [/*]

New:

  • 60 BPM → 160 BPM

    [/*]

New Heart Rate Status Tiers

  • Normal

    [/*]

  • Anxious

    [/*]

  • Panicked

    [/*]

  • Distressed

    [/*]

Hunt Changes

  • Demons can now hunt when players are Anxious

    [/*]

  • All ghosts can hunt when players are Panicked or Distressed

    [/*]

Additionally, hunt chances are no longer fixed once a threshold is reached. The higher your heart rate rises, the greater the chance of a hunt occurring, creating a more dynamic escalation of danger throughout the investigation.

Dedicated Headgear Slot

Headgear no longer occupies one of your inventory slots.

A new dedicated equipment slot has been added specifically for head-mounted gear, ensuring that inventory capacity modifiers won't remove your ability to use a headlamp.

Additional notes:

  • Holding the drop key will drop your headgear

    [/*]

  • Headgear functionality remains on its own keybind

    [/*]

  • Inventory capacity settings do not affect headgear

    [/*]

Laptop Overhaul

The contract laptop has received a significant usability update.

You can now:

  • Purchase equipment

    [/*]

  • Organize your loadout

    [/*]

  • Select equipment to bring into a contract

    [/*]

All from a single interface without needing to run and back and forth between the crate and your laptop!

Headbob Reduction Setting

One of the most requested accessibility features is finally here.

A new Headbob Reduction setting has been added, significantly reducing camera movement while preserving multiplayer animation synchronization.

This feature is currently considered experimental and may continue to improve in future updates.

Spectral Affixer Changes (Cleanse)

The Spectral Affixer has been adjusted to reduce unnecessary punishment on higher difficulties.

You can now only enter the exact number of characteristics required for a scan.

Examples:

  • If a scan requires 2 characteristics, you may only enter 2 total

    [/*]

  • If a scan requires 3 characteristics, you may only enter 3 total

    [/*]

This change applies regardless of difficulty settings and removes situations where higher difficulties could unintentionally punish players simply for entering additional information.

Additional Changes

Contract Guide

  • The contract guide on your cellphone now displays active difficulty modifiers

    [/*]

Grace Period

  • Added a 5-second grace period when returning from the Death Room

    [/*]

Session Codes

  • Removed ambiguous characters from invite codes

    [/*]

Hiding Spots

  • Adjusted various hiding spots throughout multiple locations

    [/*]

Identify Mode

  • Various gameplay improvements and balancing adjustments

    [/*]

EMF

  • Low-grade EMF can now occasionally remain after ghost events

    [/*]

Remote Temperature Sensor

  • Cost reduced from $150 to $90

    [/*]

  • Temperature updates now occur faster

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Fixed an issue where the Doppelganger could occasionally hunt from outside its favorite room under rare circumstances

    [/*]

  • Fixed the Pickup Truck clipping into a fence on Abaddon Hallows East

    [/*]

  • Various stability fixes

    [/*]

Thank you for all of the feedback and suggestions that helped shape this update!

We're excited to see the custom challenges, chaotic investigations, and creative difficulty presets the community comes up with.

See you on the other side.

-The Other Side Development Team

items.title: Five horror games to keep the fear alive after Halloween
items.summary: Halloween may be over but that doesn
items.content:
Halloween may be over but that doesn't mean the scares have to stop.

If you're not ready to pack up the pumpkins and call it a season, these five horror games will keep your adrenaline pumping …

This item is available in full to subscribers.

If you're a print and web subscriber, but do not yet have an online account, click here to create one.

Click here to see your options for becoming a subscriber.

If you're not ready to pack up the pumpkins and call it a season, these five horror games will keep your adrenaline pumping through November and beyond. From ghost hunting with friends to diving into the darkest corners of your mind or the ocean, this lineup will keep the lights on and your nerves shot.

The name of this game translates to "fear of ghosts." If you love a good 'whodunit' but wish it came with a side of heart-pounding terror, "Phasmophobia" is the game for you. This paranormal investigation horror game from Kinetic Games lets you and up to three friends play ghost hunters in a variety of haunted locations from cozy suburban homes to sprawling asylums. Right now, "Phasmophobia" is having a Blood Moon event for Halloween. The developers often try to have fun challenges during main holidays. In-game screenshot by Whisper Edwards / Gulf Coast Media = 728 ){ var m3_u = (location.protocol=='https:'?'https://gulfcoastbanners.creativecirclemedia.com/www/delivery/ajs.php':'https://gulfcoastbanners.creativecirclemedia.com/www/delivery/ajs.php'); var m3_r = Math.floor(Math.random()*99999999999); if (!document.MAX_used) document.MAX_used = ','; document.write (" "); } //]]>--> "); } //]]>--> = 728 ){ var m3_u = (location.protocol=='https:'?'https://gulfcoastbanners.creativecirclemedia.com/www/delivery/ajs.php':'https://gulfcoastbanners.creativecirclemedia.com/www/delivery/ajs.php'); var m3_r = Math.floor(Math.random()*99999999999); if (!document.MAX_used) document.MAX_used = ','; document.write (" "); } //]]>--> "); } //]]>-->

I like games where I have to put the puzzle together by investigating clues, remembering each ghost's unique mechanics and evidence, and "Phasmophobia" delivers that thrill perfectly every time I play. It's like an escape room — once the ghost starts hunting you, you're locked in and have to rely on your instincts and the facts to survive.

Armed with EMF readers, spirit boxes, video cameras and a healthy dose of denial, your job is to figure out which of the 24 types of ghosts is haunting the location. Each ghost comes with unique mechanics that make every hunt different and sometimes horrifyingly unpredictable. A Revenant moves painfully slow until it sees you, then turns into a blur of murderous intent. A Demon can hunt instantly without warning. A Yurei quietly drains your sanity and the Deogen? It always knows where you are. You can't hide.

Players can communicate through voice chat, which makes things more immersive and terrifying because the ghosts can hear you. Shout your friend's name at the wrong time and you might just provoke something that doesn't like being talked to.

There's a full set of ghost-hunting gear and cursed objects to experiment with and every completed investigation earns cash and experience to unlock new tools and maps. With constant updates and new maps on the way including the upcoming Nell's Diner in November, "Phasmophobia" keeps evolving and keeps players screaming. As a ghost hunter in "Phasmophobia," your job is to gather evidence such as ghost writing, the presence of ghost orbs and more. You can also find 'cursed objects' such as tarot cards, a voodoo doll and even a monkey paw which you can use. Be warned using a cursed object may hurt more than help. = 728 ){ var m3_u = (location.protocol=='https:'?'https://gulfcoastbanners.creativecirclemedia.com/www/delivery/ajs.php':'https://gulfcoastbanners.creativecirclemedia.com/www/delivery/ajs.php'); var m3_r = Math.floor(Math.random()*99999999999); if (!document.MAX_used) document.MAX_used = ','; document.write (" "); } //]]>--> "); } //]]>--> In-game screenshot by Whisper Edwards / Gulf Coast Media = 728 ){ var m3_u = (location.protocol=='https:'?'https://gulfcoastbanners.creativecirclemedia.com/www/delivery/ajs.php':'https://gulfcoastbanners.creativecirclemedia.com/www/delivery/ajs.php'); var m3_r = Math.floor(Math.random()*99999999999); if (!document.MAX_used) document.MAX_used = ','; document.write (" "); } //]]>--> "); } //]]>-->

All the "Silent Hill" games are worth playing but "Silent Hill 2" remains the crown jewel of the series and one of the most psychologically disturbing horror stories ever made.

It follows James Sunderland, a widower who receives a letter from his dead wife calling him to the eerie town of Silent Hill. What follows is a descent into guilt, grief and torment that never gives you clear answers — just more questions. That's part of what makes it so haunting.

The sound design alone is nightmare fuel. The fog-choked streets, the relentless whisper of static, the heavy footsteps of something you'd rather not see — it all builds dread in a way few games ever have. Then there's Pyramid Head, one of gaming's most iconic monsters, representing punishment in its most brutal form.

items.title: Ghost of Yotei: Twin Wolves, Twin Hearts Walkthrough
items.summary: Learn how to find Mad Goro for the mission Twin Wolves, Twin Hearts in Ghost of Yotei. Atsu and Jubei are now working as one to defeat the Oni
items.content:
Learn how to find Mad Goro for the mission Twin Wolves, Twin Hearts in Ghost of Yotei. Atsu and Jubei are now working as one to defeat the Oni. But in order to find a way in, they’ll need to find the madman that escaped the Oni’s castle.

After escaping the Oni Raider attack on the bridge , you’ll need to meet Jubei at the Northern Matsumae Camp in Ishikari Plane.

As you travel there, you’re going to run into the Masked Man’s Quarry. This quarry is inhabited by Oni Raiders and you’ll need to clear them out to liberate the quarry.

The raiders here are more elite soldiers and will be more difficult to take down. As you clear the camp, be sure to go inside their tents to loot any materials inside.

For your efforts, you’ll gain access to an Altar of Reflection and can safely meet up with Jubei. Don’t forget to loot the pile of materials and chests you also get as a reward.

After going inside the Matsumae camp, you’ll be able to find Jubei and Commander Wada in the large tend with the four banners in front of it.

Click or tap the image to zoom in After the cutscene, follow Jubei to the stables to begin the quest Twin Wolves, Twin Hearts. Word is going around that an eccentric priest is at the summit of a mountain-top shrine.

Follow Jubei on horseback until you reach the Azure Wind Shrine. Look for the alcove and help Jubei up so you two can start your climb to the shrine.

You’ll reach a camp full of bounty hunters. Defeat them, loot the chests in the area, then follow Jubei to the burned bridge.

To reach the other side, go to the left of the bridge and look for a tree branch you can grapple onto. Go across, grapple onto another branch ahead, then climb up to get to the other side of the bridge.

Grapple onto the loose part of the bridge and pull it off to clear the way for Jubei. Go into the cave ahead to start your way to the shrine.

As you go through the cave, you’ll fall down a bridge. Up ahead is a chest, keep this in mind for later.

Go outside and platform your way down the path until you see Jubei. To the left of him is the cave exit where you’ll find that chest you missed earlier. Grapple across and swing to the other cliff and climb up.

When you reach the other side, Jubei will go to the right. Go to the left and loot the chest inside the cave to get some Oni Raider masks. After that, follow Jubei and continue climbing up the mountain.

items.title: All Kitsune Fox Statue Puzzle Solutions
items.summary: You have many puzzles to solve during your hunt for the Kitsune in Ghost of Yotei. The tricky Yotei Six member protects his trade using clever symbols and
items.content:
You have many puzzles to solve during your hunt for the Kitsune in Ghost of Yotei . The tricky Yotei Six member protects his trade using clever symbols and statues, but puzzles are meant to be solved. Here are all the Kitsune Fox Statue Puzzle Solutions in Ghost of Yotei.

Blood on the Snow is the first mission in Teshio Ridge that pits you against Kitsune Fox Statue Puzzles. Here’s how you can solve all three.

To solve the first puzzle, approach the wall between the two torches where the carved figures of two foxes stand on either side of the Nine Tails symbol.

Examining it causes Atsu to remark that the statues appear to match the ones on the lanterns . This is your clue on how to solve the door puzzle.

Look toward the brazier and pick up the burning torch .

Next, light the two lanterns that have fox statues . Once those lanterns are lit (and no others), a small passage appears under the fox statues on the wall. Interact with it to duck under and crawl forward until you reach the other side.

On either side of the door are empty pedestals, and next to those are carved fox statues . To solve the puzzle, you must examine the details of the foxes:

The fox statue to the left of the door is raising its left paw, and the one on the right is raising its right paw. You need to find fox statues that match and place them on the pedestal .

Look nearby for two other wooden foxes. Behind the fox statue on the left side of the door , when facing it directly, is a fox raising its left paw. Place it on the left pedestal.

The second fox statue is to the left of the training dummies and brazier . Place it on the right pedestal.

With that, the door makes a noise and releases some dust. Approach and press R2 to open the door and leave the area.

The third Fox Statue puzzle in Blood on the Snow appears after leaving the platforming section, later in the mission. Look for the wall with four fox statues sitting on pedestals.

Examine the statue holding the lantern in the middle. Atsu mentions the symbols, which she still can't understand. But you should take note that there are four small symbols on the pedestal , and each of these symbols can be found under the fox statues .

The pedestals can also be turned by hand , suggesting that the foxes need to point a certain way. You must solve the puzzle to progress, but the only way to do it is to finally understand what the symbols mean. Here's how:

items.title: Borderlands 4 Review – Break on Through to the Other Side
items.content:
S ix years of development, over double the budget of Borderlands 3 , arguably more controversy before launch, thanks to doubts about its pricing – Borderlands 4, everyone. Given the backlash against the three-quel’s story and characters, all eyes are on Gearbox to step up and revitalise the franchise that put looter shooters on the map.

After about 60 hours or so and reaching Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode Tier 5, I’m happy to report that they’ve succeeded, for the most part. Our story begins, as they all do, on a planet embroiled in mayhem, even as Order threatens to overwhelm all.

"The overwhelming impression from the campaign isn’t just that Gearbox wants to move on from Borderlands 3 but also to establish this as somewhat of a new start."

Kairos is in somewhat of an uprising against the Timekeeper, which is a nice way of saying that everyone has their own pockets of resistance with little to no impact. As the Vault Hunter, be it Vex, Rafa, Amon or Harlowe, you’re someone captured and Bolted by the Order due to the predisposition to chaos. It’s only with the help of the Crimson Resistance that you escape, though ultimately, it’s ECHO-4 that keeps the Timekeeper from taking control, Harbinger-style.

You’ll meet up with some returning characters like Claptrap, Amara, Zane and Moxxi, and they’re as you might remember them, just far less grating. The newcomers take on important roles, and thankfully, they’re substantial enough to warrant some interest. Rush of the Outlanders comes across as positivity incarnate, but can get emotionally bogged down. Defiant Calder carries on the fight against the Order despite effectively being outlawed by the Augers. Levaine, as developed as she is (owing to her history with Zane), is probably the weakest character-wise, but her socialite-attempting-to-adjust-to-the-badlands antics can be amusing.

Other characters inevitably pop up, and for what it’s worth, not a single one drove me to mute voice-overs in the settings. It isn’t to say that there aren’t corny lines or somewhat forced memes. And while I liked being able to approach main missions in just about any order, spending a few hours with a core group of characters and then moving on to the next region to temporarily forget about them felt off at times.

There are also the usual plot holes, some even more egregious given what the Timekeeper is capable of, and the campaign missions still involve a lot of “collect this, pull that switch, etc.” Get used to the new “grapple object and throw it at a thing” mechanic – it will resurface often. Notable exceptions abound – boarding a driller as it circles a Ripper encampment or one particular set piece that may be the coolest in the franchise for as long as it lasts. But these are also punctuated by a lot of standing around, waiting for the other character to get their dialogue out as you follow them around. Running away while hearing them over the radio only works so much, unfortunately, but at least the cutscenes, whenever they may arise, are well-made.

The overwhelming impression from the campaign isn’t just that Gearbox wants to move on from Borderlands 3 but also to establish this as somewhat of a new start. Yet when some of the most interesting threads of the overarching narrative are featured, however briefly, the overwhelming gap between each release and how long it’ll take to develop them further can leave a hardcore fan wanting.

"More than simply filling environments with stuff to do or collect, Kairos encourages venturing out and discovering things. Yes, some of these activities aren’t exactly the most inventive – Guardians who missed protecting Ghost while he hacks into a thing, rejoice, because that’s back on the menu – but they work well enough."

For quite some time, Gearbox has discussed the size and scale of Kairos, the seamless travel between zones, and the more dynamic nature of it all. With those Digirunners materializing wherever one pleases, it was difficult not to get a Destiny vibe from it all.

However, this is perhaps the biggest step forward for the franchise, both in terms of immersion and gameplay. The novelty of seamlessly traversing from the Fade Fields and their lush plains (which fits with most inhabitants being former farmers) to the dusty reaches and barren wastes of Carcadia Burn is cool. Above all else, though, Kairos feels alive. You won’t just run into enemies patrolling about, muttering how this is good work when you can get it.

Outlanders will be busy doing push-ups and doing Outlander things; Augers will get into fights with wild animals or Order forces (and sometimes reward you for helping out). The Order doesn’t just randomly drop enemies in your wake – they have outposts, which you can assail. Between the collectables, unlockable safehouses, Silos which allow for hunting Vault Fragments, Contracts, and side activities like Propaganda Speakers or Crawlers, there’s a lot to do, and that’s not even factoring in some of the side quests. Your mileage may vary, of course, but I liked the early murder-mystery chain, cheesy CSI Miami one-liners and all.

More than simply filling environments with stuff to do or collect, Kairos encourages venturing out and discovering things. Yes, some of these activities aren’t exactly the most inventive – Guardians who missed protecting Ghost while he hacks into a thing, rejoice, because that’s back on the menu – but they work well enough.

The Crawlers are a good example – it’s similar to climbing a tower in an old-school Far Cry, except you also have to carry a battery to release some vent clamps for the shiny bauble. The twist is that you can’t clamber or climb while carrying it, so some fancy throwing will be necessary on top of the traversal. These activities – and many others – award SDU, which expands your inventory slots, max ammo for each weapon type, and more, meaning that they’re worth going out of your way for, but not mandatory.
